mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where GDP growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which negatively impacts stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where the federal funds rate exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and economic activity, which negatively impacts stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where the unemployment rate exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where industrial production growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts and GDP growth are both increasing, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where housing starts and GDP growth are both increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and inflation rate are both increasing, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which negatively impacts stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where the federal funds rate and inflation rate are both increasing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strengthening labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic activity, which positively impacts stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where payroll employment growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales and GDP growth are both increasing, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during an expansion regime.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where retail sales and GDP growth are both increasing during an expansion regime.
